newsitem.title: USA: European lead battery market seen growing 2-3 pct.
newsitem.headline: European lead battery market seen growing 2-3 pct.

text.p: Demand for lead-acid batteries in Western and Central Europe will grow two to three percent between 1997 and 1998, Raymond Kubis, managing director of Belgium's Doyen-Uranio Battery Group said.

"It is true that many changes are pulling and pushing our battery industry in Europe, however, the markets in total are growing at or above historical rates," Kubis said in prepared remarks for the Battery Council International meeting in San Diego this week.
Auto and industrial lead-acid batteries account for over 70 percent of global lead consumption.
The European market for lead-acid batteries was worth some $3.3 billion last year, two-thirds of this comprising starter batteries totaling 60 million units in Western and Central Europe.
The total includes 35 million replacement batteries and 17 million original equipment batteries in Western Europe, and an estimated 8 million batteries in Central Europe.

"In total, the outlook is for 2-3 percent real growth in the lead acid battery markets in Europe, with industrial batteries for stationary applications and starter batteries for Central Europe, and some original equipment regions showing the highest growth," Kubis said.
Replacement battery demand in Western Europe is forecast to grow but at historically lower 1-2 percent rates.
Further consolidation among the medium and small sized battery makers is expected, and there will be new or additional producers' involvement in Europe.
Battery making in Europe is dominated by America's Exide Corp which along with BTR-Hawker, and Varta AB, have 65 percent of the European market.
Exide has estimated European sales of $1.1 billion, with BTR-Hawker $600 million, and Varta $500 million out of the total market of $3.3 billion, Kubis said.
